pitch_detail.notes: Follow the crack up toward the chimney and set the belay at the chimney's base. Gear used was a #2, a #3 and a nut. It may be possible to run this together with the next pitch.

Stem and climb the box chimney, then break out left near its top and work up a short face section to a small stance. Loose blocks sit here (the only ones on the route) and should be pulled off. Belay above them in a solid crack; a single #3 plus other pieces is enough, since the second #3 ends up in the anchor.

Climb the clean, sharply cut corner to a rest, where you can also belay out to the right. Continue straight up the splitter crack; it narrows and steepens, and face holds then lead to the top. The belay is set well back on the ledge.

review.changed: Wrote all 3 pitches with grades and gear hints; no lengths or bolt counts stated, none written.
review.other_findings: None; descent (walk off right) matches stored.

pitch_detail.notes: Pick any of the many hand cracks in the corner system and follow them to a small perch about halfway up the system.
Keep going up the right-hand face, which is covered in hand cracks of various lines; you drift right as you climb but almost any path works. The belay is closer to hanging, taken wherever is easiest.
The cracks steepen slightly and give sustained jamming with good position. Staying on the far-right cracks leads to an exit around the arete onto a roomy ledge.
Climb the corner leaving the ledge (a bit grainy), then angle up and left as the slope eases, taking the easiest line toward the top.
Continue up and left toward the summit. A small corner takes you nearly to the top, then a few jugs lead onto the summit block.

review.changed: Wrote all 5 pitches with grades and lengths (m as stated).

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the red streak up and left past a pocket that takes a cam, then on sparse gear to a wide ledge. Move to the ledge's far right end and belay above a small sapling. Runout.
Go up and right past a small overlap, then work back left to a broken stance under the wide roof/flake. Protection is reasonable (PG). Larger pieces help build the belay here.
Step onto the red slab past a pocket (cam) and one quarter-inch bolt. A short runout leads to easier cracks, then step right to belay at Two Tree ledge.

Climb easy corners, then a diagonal hand/fist crack heading left across polished gold rock, then up to a big ledge. After this, 4th class scrambling for about 300 ft reaches the summit of Falls Ridge East.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches. Rappels not listed station by station (none written).
review.other_findings: descent_text is null on the row; the text gives a descent: from the summit follow the northeast ridge to an easy gully traversing back along the base (about 40 min), or a forested gully to climber's left below the summit headwall.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in the left-angling flake and work into the right side of the A-frame feature capped by a roof. Engaging climbing with sporty gear. Pull the roof and belay at bolts that are in questionable shape.

Step left to an odd groove-crack and follow it to a sloping ledge (optional belay). Then a steep stemming/finger-crack box leads to a good bolt and a big roof. The roof is hard; easier climbing past it reaches a good two-bolt anchor.
The corner you see from the ground: a few bouldery steps lead into a sustained corner groove. Belay on a stance in a dike.

Continue up the corner with climbing that gets harder. At the roof, exit on its right side into a layback feature, follow it until stepping right into another crack system is sensible, and climb that to a good two-bolt anchor at a hanging stance. Some rate this pitch as hard as 5.11b.
Go up and left into the obvious corner full of flakes, ribs and grooves. Above the large flake at its top, step right to a small ledge and belay.

From the previous belay, locate the prow directly below the Finger, with a tight V-groove on its left that opens into a hand crack. Work up and left to it, climb it to a good ledge on top and belay. Technical shimmying.

Step right and climb the crack along the right side of the Finger; some sporty moves low for the grade. The crack looks wide above but a solid #3 fits once you stand in it. Belay anywhere along the North Ridge.

review.changed: Wrote 7 pitches. Listed grades are the topo's; the climbers who wrote it felt most pitches ran about a grade harder (lichen, flared cracks). Omitted the scrambling to the summit block (a couple of short finishes, 5.8 or 5.7).
review.other_findings: descent_text null on the row; text gives none.

pitch_detail.notes: A short hand crack up the left side of the big chimney leads to a sandy, sloping ledge with loose rocks scattered on it.
Loose, sandy scrambling on blocky ground for roughly 100 ft until the rock cleans up at the chimney's top. Rope up or not as you judge.
Head left up easy ledges to a nice layback onto a narrow ledge; a clean chimney sits at its west end.
Squeeze up the chimney, then follow the narrow ridge behind with great exposure, finishing with a flake move to the tiny summit.

rappel_detail.station: about 10 ft below the summit on the southeast side
rappel_detail.notes: Brings you down to the loose, sandy class 3 section. Sharp rock here has nearly cut a rope, so weigh rappelling against downclimbing.

rappel_detail.station: on the east wall of the large chimney
rappel_detail.notes: A short rappel that gets you below the pitch 1 hand crack. Mind rope-cutting edges.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches and a 2-station rappel list.
review.other_findings: descent_text null on the row; the text gives two rappels (above).

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the crack/corner straight up to a belay on a big block or ramp that leads toward the next pitch. An approach pitch of about 45 m comes first.
Climb a slabby ramp to a corner, follow the corner up and left, and belay just under the crux pitch.
The crux. Steep corner cracks with good gear, belaying at a stance (a .3 to #1 Camelot works there).
Follow the arete and crack systems to the top, then easy snow ramp to a belay on a slung block or tree.
Easy ridge scrambling: go up and left from the belay around the rock called the bunny ears, then up and right with an unprotected traverse to a so-so belay spot before the next pitch.
Tougher snow, then fun ridge romping to a pyramid-shaped rock that makes a great sling anchor.
Ridge climbing; extend all your pieces because rope drag is the main difficulty.
More ridge romping up to the summit. Protects well, but loose rock increases toward the top.

review.changed: Wrote 8 pitches; the ~45 m approach pitch is mentioned in P1. Grades listed for pitches 1-5 follow each description's trailing line; P6-8 ungraded. Lengths are approximate (~).
review.other_findings: Row grade M6 but the crux pitch is stated as M7. Pitches 6-8 are optional to rope (competent parties may move together).

pitch_detail.notes: Steep start on good holds into some tricky mantles, then finish up a short finger crack. Traverse up and right to the bolted anchor.
Long slab straight up from the anchor, a tricky roof pull, then on to the top of the wall and a two-bolt anchor. 21 bolts on the pitch.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches. Descent: three rappels down the neighbouring route to the left, but no stations listed, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a wide crack to a ledge, clip a bolt, then stem and jam a corner into a splitter flake and crack. When the crack ends go up through a roof (bolts) and finish up a slab to a semi-hanging belay. Stands on its own as a single pitch.

Start on low-angle shattered rock that takes good gear, to a right-leaning right-facing dihedral. Climb the dihedral (mostly bolted), alternating jams and face holds on the right, pull a bulge near the top, and finish on technical dikes to an anchor at a large flake.
This is the first pitch of the Emperor.
Follow the obvious dike out to the right.

Hard moves off the belay lead up and left into a corner, which you follow to the giant flake above (watch rope drag). Traverse out right and back onto the face, then right again at the bush to end in the groove.
The easiest pitch: a right-facing corner to the belay.
Hard moves off the belay past a few bolts, then into a dike with more bolts. Leave the dike aiming for the roof and finish at a stance.

Climb the corner and make delicate moves out left at the top, then two more bolts above. At the top of this section two options: right goes directly up the dihedral with strange footwork or knee bars (about 5.12+, the line freed first), left is slightly harder and needs a horizontal mantle.
Climb through the roof, then directly right toward the obvious bulge mid-face. Step down to better footholds off poor hands, then continue right on easy ground until you meet What's Up Bubb.
The crux pitch of What's Up Bubb.
Go left off the belay through the grainy roof and follow the obvious tufa to the belay.
Go right around the corner to stepped dihedrals and follow bolts for about 50 ft, then up knobs and broken ground to the belay.
Easy climbing to link back with What's Up Bubb and, further up, the upper two pitches of the Emperor to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote the 11 pitches the text describes (no lengths stated). No rappel table: descent is described only as rappelling to the bottom of pitch 9 then following What's Up Bubb's rappels, with a 70 m rope and tag line.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches 14, text lists 11 (P11 folds in the Emperor's upper two). Stored descent says the lower stations are all bolted; the text says rappel from the top to the base of pitch 9.

pitch_detail.notes: Start on Ikigai. Crux off the ground to the top of a chockstone, then easy scrambling to the back of the chimney and a bolt. Stem up past three more bolts to a two-bolt anchor. About 100 ft (a rough estimate).

Scramble up the gully about 20 ft, then a short face to an awkward mantle onto a ramp. Follow the ramp up and right past another bolt to the base of a left-facing dihedral; jam the widening hand crack (5.10), then step down and left to a two-bolt anchor on a good ledge. About 70 ft.

The Seam. Easy ground past a couple of bolts (5.10a to 5.11a depending on height), then 5.9 cracks on medium cams to a ledge. Tiptoe up the technical seam past five more bolts to a sloping belay. About 80 ft.

Here the route leaves Ikigai's Dave Slab pitches (those remain an option). Head straight up a right-facing, right-trending dihedral to a #5 BD layback (5.7 R), or sneak out right on a thin flake (5.9) to a two-bolt anchor on a ledge. About 90 ft.

Continue up the dihedral into a juggy golden chimney that becomes a face, then cut hard right along a ledge to rejoin Ikigai above its mantle move. Easy climbing but a big swing for the second. About 90 ft.
Ikigai's crux pitch: hand-size gear leads to steep bolted face and a two-bolt belay on a good ledge. About 80 ft.

Zig Zag Pitch. From the belay's right side go up an easy right-facing dihedral, cut left through a golden bulge (crux) past two bolts, then hard left and down a dike system to a bolt. Pull onto the ramp, clip another bolt, downclimb about 10 ft and climb left into a left-facing dihedral (awkward, 5.10+). Finger and hand crack up the pillar to a two-bolt belay beside a loose block. About 90 ft.
Climb under the roof and exit left into powerful, exposed laybacking past bolts to a right-leaning ramp, ending on a good ledge at a left-facing corner. About 100 ft.

Continue up Ikigai (steep 5.9), then go well right and up to a lone bolt, an easy (5.5) downclimb ramp and a 5.9 step right onto Inseguimento Ledge. About 100 ft. Rappel option from the ledge: roughly 190 ft down and climber's left to a two-bolt anchor on a long ledge.

From the ledge, layback to the crack (5.11a), through fingers and hands to a dike ledge on the right. Up and right into a thought-provoking corner (crux) then more hard climbing (5.11a). At the big hollow flake either go straight past a bolt to link with the next pitch or belay out left above a bush. About 100 ft.

Climb the big hollow flake, then a thin finger crack to a bolt (5.11a) and a left-facing dihedral on medium gear. When it cuts right, go straight up and left (bolts) into the Golden Shield Headwall (crux) to a two-bolt anchor on a sloping ledge. About 80 ft.
Straight up past a bolt to thin technical gear climbing and a two-bolt belay just before the crack cuts hard right. Can link with the next pitch but you want the gear for this one. About 70 ft.

Easy climbing along a right-trending low-angle dihedral past a couple of bushes, then fingers as the crack turns vertical, then tips (crux) and maybe a medium piece, to a two-bolt anchor at a stance. About 110 ft.

Walking on Sunshine. Up the left-hand crack (bolts), then hard right to a thin crack (crux, bolts) to a ledge under a prominent roof. Medium then tips/finger cams to the roof, layback out it, then glorious laybacking on golden granite past a couple of bolts, thin and medium gear, more bolts, to a flake and a two-bolt anchor at a good stance. About 130 ft.
The Trio: climb the golden double dikes, escaping left to a two-bolt anchor on a good ledge at the top of the Golden Shield Headwall. About 90 ft. Lower-angle climbing follows to the top.

Straight up on bolts just right of a bottoming crack. As that crack cuts right past a bad bolt, go up and left past a bolt (5.9) and a short crack to a good belay atop a prominent pillar. About 90 ft.

Up and left to a high first bolt to join a long dike; follow it until you can step right (bolt) to an easy hand crack that curves left, then straight up the face (bolt) to a two-bolt anchor on a good ledge. About 130 ft.
Climb either of two cracks straight up to a bolt, then step left into a left-facing corner with fingers and hands to a nice ledge and two-bolt anchor. About 60 ft.
Continue straight up, trending left to join Ikigai on a big ledge, then easy climbing to the summit tree of Ikigai. About 180 ft.

review.changed: Wrote all 19 pitches. Lengths left in the notes (as approximate feet) because the text says they are rough guesses. No rappel table: only a partial rappel option from Inseguimento Ledge is given.
review.other_findings: None. Pitches 1-3 are shared with Ikigai.

pitch_detail.notes: Ice about 55 m long.
About 60 m, mostly WI2 with one WI3 step.
About 60 m, WI2 and perhaps slightly harder in places.
Easier, WI2- with mixed snow. From here you can continue or exit climber's left via 3rd class ledges to get off the peak.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches; lengths per the text; pitch length and difficulty depend on how thick the ice is. No rappel table (V-threads mentioned only in general).
review.other_findings: None. Row grade WI3 M1-2; text only mentions a WI3 step.

pitch_detail.notes: Start off a small rock tower separated from the main face and make a short hand traverse along a crack over a steep gully to a big ledge. Walk left to a gear belay.
Hand crack in the left wall; dirty in places but good. Belay behind a giant chockstone.
Three-dimensional stemming from the belay. Links with the next pitch using a 70 m rope.
Delicate climbing on small gear to a nice crack system. Leave Cinco de Mayo and move out right to a bolted anchor at a stance.
Follow the obvious chicken-head-covered flake up and right: 5 bolts, with gear and a slung chicken head. Bolted belay.

Easy flake to a small ledge, then a hollow flake with a good crack, a roof with a finger crack turning to side pulls and crimps to the next roof, then flakes left and up to a large dike and bolted belay. 8 bolts plus gear; extend pieces carefully. The crux moves can be pulled through.
Traverse right along the dike past 5 bolts and one #0.5 placement near the end. Bolted belay before the junction with the West Face route.
A face move right joins the West Face crack; a great hand crack on the right side of the flake leads to a great ledge with a piton belay.
A short but burly crack leads to a great hand crack and a ledge in an alcove under an overhang. Gear belay. The grade is given as 5.8 to 5.10.
Awesome moves past the roof to a splitter to the summit. The bolted rap anchor on the far side of loose blocks can serve as a belay.

review.changed: Wrote 10 pitches with lengths from feet. Pitches 8-10 may be linked in any combination; the best ledge is atop P8. Pitch 3 and 4 can be linked with a 70 m rope.

pitch_detail.notes: Up flakes to the top of a pinnacle, clip a bolt, then face moves into a crack/undercling. Take that out right and layback flaky rock to the anchor, on a slab just below the obvious crack that leads to P2. About 200 ft; grade is an estimate.
Climb the crack, then go left around the arete. Clip a bolt and follow thin cracks that eventually trend up and right to a ledge belay. Length not remembered; grade an estimate.
Series of cracks: stay right, then move left via a nice finger crack to a ledge with splitters above; climb them and continue up. A long pitch, possibly about 200 ft; grade uncertain (about 5.9).
Go left off the belay toward the obvious corner above; belay where the angle eases. Maybe 120 ft; grade an estimate.
Several ways to go; the corner and then left to the summit. Short, maybe 50 ft.

review.changed: Wrote 5 pitches; grades and lengths are the original authors' estimates; P3 grade left off and lengths only where stated firmly.

pitch_detail.notes: Start a few feet left of the 4th class gully of the neighbouring route; head up low-angle face into an open dihedral, over a small roof, to a bolted belay.
Head hard left along a dike, gain a crack trending back up right, and at its top move left on xenolith inclusions to a scooped ledge with a bolted anchor.

Face cracks and right-facing dihedral cracks up to a roof, stem wide past it, and follow cracks and features to a giant feldspar dike. Pass a bolt below the dike and an intermediate anchor above it, then traverse left along the dike 30-40 ft to another bolted anchor.
Follow the wide crack from the anchor (no wide gear or climbing needed) to another bolted anchor.

Continue up the crack, past an old leaper piton; the cracks become discontinuous but the climbing is easy, so shift between crack systems. Build a gear anchor on a small stance directly below a large bulge. The first bolt of the next pitch is 15-20 ft up past the bulge.

Climb up to the bolt using surprisingly good holds over the steep bulge, then traverse left with long runouts, crossing several crack systems, and build a gear anchor where possible. Very runout and tricky route-finding.
Keep moving left across more crack systems, find the single bolt, and continue up to a bolted anchor under a steep headwall. Questing and runout.
Climb past fat bolts to a dark hand-size crack cutting the overhanging headwall, bolt-protected. An optional anchor sits just above the overhanging crack section.
Follow bolts up and right over steep but featured terrain, then more bolts up a stemming groove to a bolted anchor.

Crack and groove with sparse protection at the start that improves at the flakes. Continue up another stemming groove with some bolts to a triangular roof alcove. Pull through on good jams, follow an easy leftward crack, then cut back right on lower-angle face to a bolted anchor on a rounded arete.

Go right up a ramp to the base of a steep bolted groove, stem up it to a bolted anchor on a sloping ledge. It is more comfortable to climb about 30 ft past that anchor and build a gear anchor among blocks on the bivy ledge. Then scramble to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 11 labelled pitches (the text splits pitch 8 into 8a and 8b, both ending at an anchor) with lengths from feet.
review.other_findings: Stored pitch count 10, text describes 11 (8a and 8b). Long runouts on moderate pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: From the right end of the long low roof at the west end of the face, climb discontinuous cracks, cross The Knobivore, go up slabs to the left side of a gray slab between two shallow corner systems. Up the left corner to the roof, then the cracks above to a belay with tricky gear on a spacious ledge at a left-facing corner.

Weave up the corner, step right to turn the roof, up slabs, turn another roof on the right, and follow cracks to the big roof. Step left to a crack through the roof (fat fingers), but do not climb it: step left again and take the hand crack through the roof. Belay at an adequate stance just above.

Step left and up to a crack on the right; follow it up, trending right, to another small roof; pull it, then up and right to a secure belay among colossal flakes. Above, the angle eases and the terrain turns mostly 2nd and 3rd class.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches, no grades or lengths stated. The easy terrain above (the text calls it P4, P5) is left out; it is a romp north with a few downclimbing moves to a sandy area, then an exit by slabs and a gully.

pitch_detail.notes: Short face climb to a vertical crack system just left of a more broken one. Belay on an ample ledge system.

Traverse left on slabby ground, then up and left to reach the gully/corner system above the stacked-block mess, and up the corner. Avoid the left-facing corner/arch on the right: it relies on a loose, person-size block.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; only P1 length stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Just right of the 200+ ft left-facing corner, scamper up to a smaller corner/crack system, through the small roof at its top, tiptoe up and left to another crack system, and left again when it ends, to the crack just right of the big corner's edge. Belay in small huecoed stances under a small roof.
Continue up the crack on the left through the roof to double cracks (the crux) and a belay ledge on the left.
Short overhanging crack over the belay, then step right and into the overhanging left-leaning slot in the roof band. Belay on adequate stances above or below the flat chockstone in the wide crack.
Escape option: up the gully on the left. Above the chockstone, traverse hard left into the gray gully and up to a belay in a sandy corridor. Easy but crumbly. About 100 ft.

Direct option: from vertical parallel hand/finger cracks under stacked noses, climb up, step left at the first nose and up its left side, then right into a short overhanging corner crack (a #4 helps at the exit). About 50 ft more on easier ground leads to a spacious belay at a notch/groove. About 80 ft.

review.changed: Wrote P1-P3 and the two alternate fourth pitches (4a, 4b).

pitch_detail.notes: Up to the left flake, step left, climb discontinuous cracks and orange face to a belay stance at the base of a crack/flake system arching up left. Alternative: right-facing corner system; when the gear runs out, step left onto orange rock then left in cracks and flakes to the same belay (5.7 with good protection).

Up the arching crack, left where the overlap is cut by cracks, then up and left to a pair of cracks: take the hand crack that widens and curves left (not the one that heads up right on #4 Camalot, nor the corner with flowers). Up to the roof and a short awkward traverse to a stance on the right.

Angle up the right-hand crack, then difficult moves link crack systems up and right to a belay under a roof formed by a block wedged in the corner. Fixed nuts here. Alternative linking left to Gas Chromatographer: stem the inset alcove, step left to a ledge under steep cracks and flakes, then to ample ledges (about 5.9, 60 ft).
Up giant blocks and a short stout crack system until you can trend left on easier ground to the centre of the tower. Belay on ample ledges.
Scamper to the top of the tower, then 3rd class scrambling toward the northwest end of the formation.

review.changed: Wrote 5 pitches with the stated alternatives folded into notes of the pitch they replace.

pitch_detail.notes: Up and left on good cracks toward a belay just right of likely cracks through the roof.
Pull the roof at the hand crack, step left into the next crack system and up to a good stance where you can watch the second pull the roof.

Up the odd wide crack/slot (a #5 BD is handy), step left and up orange face to a crack or thin seam, then trend up and right on much easier ground, perhaps reaching the summit ridge depending on rope drag and rope length. Loose rock here needs a good trundle.
Scramble north along the ridge and down to a sandy area; then traverse the ridge north or walk the sand until the face forces you up slabs on the left, a short downclimb and a gully to the ground.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches; the last is a scramble/descent with no grade.
review.other_findings: None; descent is not stored but the text describes the walk-off.

skip_reasons.ca_eagle_peak_4_hanging_rock_5_10_ao: Garbled text; only pitches 1-2 sketched (aid 'AO', then 5.10), third pitch vague; unclear.
